sources.summary: Introduces lead versus electrode, limb and precordial systems, viewing planes, basic conduction, PQRSTU nomenclature, paper calibration and interval measurement.
limitations: Page 7 has an atrial repolarisation/depolarisation wording error.

Page 11 QTc range is a course heuristic; use contemporary qualified sex/rate/QRS-specific context, and explain Bazett limitations.
Standard 25 mm/s and 10 mm/mV are examples to check on each recording, not assumptions for every ECG.

sources.role: Optional professional reading, research context and quality improvement
sources.status: All 44 pages OCR processed; selected articles text-reviewed; all-page visual overview; not comprehensively clinically validated
sources.visualReviewLevel: All-page thumbnail overview; detailed page inspection 13,16,22,24
sources.summary: Summer 2026 professional journal includes single-ventricle care, two ECG acquisition/competency studies, conference reports, service development and careers. The two ECG studies support acquisition checks and continued practical reassessment.
limitations: Image-only PDF: OCR completed for all pages, but recognition/column order is poor on some pages, notably 5 and 34.
Only listed textReviewPages were read in full; pages 6–12,29–30,33–34,37–44 were skimmed or visually screened.
Research studies are small, institution-based observational/self-report work; do not imply causal training effectiveness or representative national error rates.
Article p24 has an experience range versus duration-table discrepancy (narrative 25–60 months; table 19 ± 11 months). Verify with authors before quoting experience statistics.
No independent verification of journal references or conference treatment claims undertaken in this audit.
Do not reproduce original journal figures or people/contact lists in the public app.

journalReadings.title: Accuracy of precordial ECG electrode placement by clinically authorised trainees in NHS practice
journalReadings.summary: A small observational study of 36 authorised trainees highlights persistent anatomical-placement errors after competency sign-off. This is context for checking acquisition before interpreting morphology.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Connect lead theory with recording-quality checks and practical reassessment; discuss sampling and measurement limitations.

journalReadings.title: ECG training, competency assessment, and perceived development needs: a cross-sectional survey
journalReadings.summary: A 40-participant convenience survey describes varied initial assessment, limited reported routine acquisition audit and support for refresher training. Self-reported preferences do not establish that any intervention improves patient outcomes.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Understand why spaced practice, acquisition checklists and feedback complement an initial sign-off.

journalReadings.title: Rhythm management in the era of remote monitoring
journalReadings.summary: Conference report discusses service opportunities, alert workload, patient engagement and uncertainty around optimal monitoring services.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Broaden basic pacing knowledge into follow-up and governance context.

journalReadings.title: Atrial fibrillation in HFpEF: what the evidence says and what is the role of wearable technologies?
journalReadings.summary: Conference report highlights the overlap of AF with HFpEF and distinguishes wearable detection from less established management applications.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Consider the clinical setting of AF beyond naming the rhythm; verify treatment statements in guidelines.

journalReadings.title: Rhythm management strategies in HCM
journalReadings.summary: Conference report frames device decisions around individual risk, potential benefits, complications and patient preferences.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Understand why an ECG pattern alone does not determine an ICD decision.

journalReadings.title: The future of patient-centred HCM care from a cardiac science perspective
journalReadings.summary: Conference report describes screening, lifelong surveillance, multidisciplinary governance and evolving scientist-led services.
journalReadings.reasonToRead: Place inherited-risk recognition within family assessment and ongoing specialist care.
